item.title: Input sought on additional protection of Alakai Wilderness on Kauai
item.description: LIHUE — The Department of Land and Natural Resources Division of Forestry and Wildlife (DOFAW) is seeking community feedback on a proposed fencing project to protect an additional 2,400 acres in the Alakai Wilderness Preserve on Kauai.

item.title: Bills seek to rein in free-roaming cat population in Hawaii
item.description: Should all cats five months or older in Hawaii be sterilized?

item.title: Senate rejects bill granting rights to watersheds, reefs
item.description: Despite strong support from environmental and Native Hawaiian stewardship groups, a bill that would recognize watersheds and coral reefs as legal persons failed to move forward in the Legislature Wednesday.

item.title: Hawaii environmental leaders condemn EPA rollback
item.description: State and local environmental leaders strongly condemned President Donald Trump’s move on Thursday to rescind a scientific finding, the loss of which effectively deregulated greenhouse gas emissions under the Environmental Protection Agency — with the state Energy Office calling it “one of the largest environmental rollbacks in U.S. history.”

item.title: Brandon Lin medals at HHSAA Swimming and Diving State Championships
item.description: LIHUE — Kauai High School senior Brandon Lin brought home medals from the 2026 K. Mark Takai Hawaii High School Athletic Association Swimming and Diving State Championships, presented by Kyo-Ya at the Kamehameha Schools-Hawaii Island, which ended Feb. 14.

item.title: KCC Culinary Arts students learn with award-winning chefs
item.description: For more than a dozen Kauai Community College students in the Garde Manger Culinary Arts class led by George Levendis, Wednesday marked the end of two days of instruction with award-winning Waikiki hotel Chef Dale Radomski and Charlie Matsuda, the executive sous chef at the Sheraton Kauai at Coconut Beach.

item.title: Bills aimed at legalizing recreational marijuana lack support
item.description: Two bills aimed at legalizing recreational marijuana — or even creating marijuana guardrails — are effectively dead, according to House Speaker Nadine Nakamura and Rep. David Tarnas, who has pushed for legalization for years.
